title: Forbes band at the Sanger Theatre and its members
summary: Hirsch worked about nine months with Forbes at the Sanger; he names the players, most now dead, and Leo Forbstein.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And you worked with who at the Sanger? I worked with Forbes. Forbes?
How long was Forbes' band in the Sanger? About nine months.
Uh-huh. Nine months or so. This is Louie Primer. Uh-huh. Yeah. Ed Fontana, Charlie Hartman. All these guys are dead.

Ed Fontana, any relation to Carl Fontana? No. No. No, no, no. Hector Fontana is his son. Ah, okay. Now, Leo Forbstein. That was his brother. His brother. Was he ever involved down here? No. Did he ever come here? No, no.

He was on the First National. He was at First National. But every one of these people, this is the only guy that I know if he's still alive. Every one of these guys are dead. So Alessandro, this guy dead. This guy dead. This guy dead. Paquet, the clarinet, there's Alessandro, there's Tony Papalia, Charlie Hartman, Fontana, Rico Condona, Johnny Detroit just died, Mike Apparello I know has been dead for quite a while, and Louis Primer's dead. Who goddamn band is dead? That's it that Blair sung Evolution of Music? That was Evolution of Music. 4-28-32. Gosh.
